positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
Cyber Security Product
C++ Windows | Multi Threaded features
DLP Product - Performed Content Inspection on files in order to obtain their content. Content was then processed by multiple threads and check for specific regular expression or pattern matches. Such matches provided an insight into the important characteristics of the files content. DLP Rules could then be applied to determine if user actions being performed should be permitted or not. 

Worked on User Space code and also Kernel code.

Unit Tests used Google Mocking.
End to End System tests were written in Robot Framework / Python

Visual Studio or windbg used for debugging issues.

Developer was involved in Designs , Implementation , Test and Documentation phases. 
Agile Methodologies used to track requirements, Work broken into Stories and tasks so progress could be tracked,

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer - USD Division (Data Storage Products)
positions.description:
During my time at EMC I worked on various software features requiring System Management and Middleware software that resides on both the EMC VNX and VNXe products. The VNX is a large end data storage product, while the VNXe is a low end data storage product. 

VNXe - Restful API mgmt stack
I was responsible for the development of a Restful API management stack (written in Java). The Rest stack provides an interface that cloud based applications can use to provision data storage on the VNXe. VNXe management features were also exposed via the stack. The Apache tomcat web server was used to handle the processing of HTTP requests. Processing included login and security logic. The Rest stack registers specific URL patterns with tomcat allowing tomcat to forward matching requests to the stack. The HTTP requests contain JSON formatted messages which are converted into Java beans. Annotations were used during the conversion to execute specific data type validation. The Java source code utilizes Spring MVC (Model, View and Controllers).The majority of the stack was automatically generated from descriptive model files and EMC based template technology. The generation was extended to include the creation of internal/external documentation describing the API.
Request processing was handled by applications that where built using the @Controller, @Service and @Dao Spring annotations. To further enhance the API’s scalability all GET path operations interfaced with a Postgres database, via JDBC queries and used Hibernate (ORM) object mapping to map Java beans to database tables and views. 
Unit tests utilized Mockito and PowerMock techniques so that tests could steer execution through the source code and achieve higher code coverage.

Prior to this project I worked on a variety of C++ based Middleware Management projects

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
I joined a small startup company called Proquent Systems. I functioned as a member of the embedded software development team focusing on the development of the Proquent’s MSSP 2820 IP Detection Point system. The MSSP 2820 is a carrier class (Compact PCI form factor) chassis based product aimed at providing enhanced wireless billing applications to End Service Providers. The MSSP 2820 utilizes a patented IP detection point technology which allows it to perform in-depth Layer 7 packet classification processing.  The MSSP is installed next to existing GGSN and PDSN equipment and allows network traffic to be analyzed and results passed up to service control applications. All embedded software for this project was developed in either C, C++ and were appropriate assembler.
Amongst my achievements were a significant contribution to the development of the chassis management server and client software. The server software provided a focal point for the control of the system. Management agents functioned on the various plug in modules and communicated to the main server over a Gigabit Ethernet channel. Many of the MSSP plug in modules executed embedded software running in a Linux Red Hat operating software environment. The embedded software functioned within a multi-threaded environment and used operating features such as semaphores, interrupt handlers, etc.
The Chassis management software interfaced with a number of different devices drivers (i.e. Flash, PCI, IPMI, etc) to utilize various hardware components. The IPMI communication protocol was used for low level chassis control and to allow for the configuration and manipulation of the Manufacturing FRU information. 
	I/O modules were developed around three processor technologies (Motorola PPC750, 8245 and the Intel IXP1240). I feature lead the development of the boot software and board level diagnostics software (including packet loopback tests, memory and register tests).

positions.title: Principal Sofware Engineer - Commworks Division - (Voice over IP)
positions.description: I worked on embedded management software for 3Com’s Total Control 2000 Voice over IP platform. The Total Control 2000 used CORBA as a means of distributing management data between platforms and servers. Also developed embedded microcode applets that were downloaded into MMC NP5410 network processors, which were used on an internal Total Control 2000 Gigabit Ethernet switching module.

positions.title: Senior Embedded Software Engineer - MSD Division - (Ethernet Switches)
positions.description: Due to my experience with Gigabit Ethernet link auto-negotiation technology 3Com transferred me to the United States where I worked on C++ based embedded management control software for a 36 port Gigabit Ethernet Link downlink module which connected into the Corebuilder 9000 Layer 3product range and manipulated its Power PC 860 processor.

positions.title: Embedded Software Engineer (WSD Division)
positions.description:
During my time at 3Com’s WSD division, I feature lead a number of projects, including the development of C++ based embedded management software for 3Com’s Super Stack II 1100 and 3300 Ethernet Switching product range. The embedded management software was managed via SNMP mibs and responded to SNMP management requests. I was team lead for the implementing management software to control 3COMs first ever Gigabit Ethernet downlink module, which connects to the 1100 and 3300 products. Other projects included working LAN Emulation for a ATM 155Mbps downlink module which connecting in the SuperStack II product and allow data traffic to flow between ATM and Ethernet based networks. 
             3Com designs its products using an Object Oriented approach techniques and documented designs using the JSP notation.
